title: Function Templates and Type Parameters
learningObjectives: Explain function templates and type parameters.
Identify template parameters and required operations.
Design a reusable generic utility or type.

understand.concept: A function template defines a family of functions using type parameters. The compiler instantiates concrete versions for compatible argument types. Generic operations still require the involved types to support those operations.
understand.whyItMatters: Templates reduce duplicated implementations for operations that are genuinely type-generic.
understand.explain: Identify the placeholder type, the operations used on it, and the type selected at each call. Test integers, floating-point values and a compatible custom type.

examples.title: Generic max
examples.code: template<class T> T larger(T a,T b){return a>b?a:b;}\n// larger(3,8) returns 8
examples.explanation: T must support comparison and return-by-value.

examples.title: Generic swap
examples.code: template<class T> void swapVals(T& a,T& b){T temp=a;a=b;b=temp;}
examples.explanation: T must support copying/assignment in this implementation.

examples.title: Identity
examples.code: template<class T> T identity(T v){return v;}\nint n=identity(7);

examples.title: Print helper
examples.code: template<class T> void print(const T& v){std::cout<<v;}\nprint(42);
examples.explanation: The type must support stream insertion.

examples.title: Generic positive part
examples.code: template<class T> T positive(T v){return v<T{}?T{}:v;}
examples.explanation: T needs comparison and value initialization.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze each Function Templates and Type Parameters example: identify parameters, requirements, deduced or explicit arguments, and instantiated behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a generic C++ utility or type demonstrating function templates and type parameters. Test two supported types, one boundary case, and one unsupported/constrained type; explain why it is or is not accepted.
hints: Begin with a concrete example before generalizing.
Name template parameters for their roles.
